messages.message: Just got here. Check in across from Tigers garage.
Tigers garage. Admin offices is where I checked in.
I'm out of pocket. Kevin giving your story a second read today

Column and then a Tigers story off of media availability.
 

 Also a six. 
 

 No notes

Writing short on Tigers moves. farmer, Collins down. Presley up
Ok cool. In clubhouse

Any advance stuff you want to work on today? Looks like we've got half the staff at Tigers. Can give you the light lift on copy for daily if you do.
Yeah I was just going to do the game story
Tigers have no comment
If it was hard news, we could cite and build an entire story out of it. Not for something like that, though.

Stuff like this is great for morning updates. And it doesn't take a lot of your time. 
 

 

 5 reasons why the Tigers didn't just give Ian Kinsler away on waivers | MLive.com http://s.mlive.com/eXscQih

For sure. But you get my point: It's added analysis and traffic at a time when nobody is reading commodity news on the Tigers, especially games. The Kinsler waiver news was read very well for us, which means there's an audience. 
 

 People want analysis.
5 young guys who have big opportunities last couple months? Ok. 5 reasons the Tigers didn't let Ian Kinsler go for free? Eh
If it's a win, we probably save it. But usually the Tigers gamer is read well the next day after wins. Losses, as you know, not so much.

So how do we respond when people aren't reading? That's what we have to figure out. 
 

 Does it require something additional in the morning or something alternative storyform? Is it something we plan a couple of morning listicle posts each week that we know are going to pop?

I thought Rondon was smart and well played yesterday. We don't need a column every day, but that thing did 20K because you responded to a topic buzzing in the fan base. Is Kinsler obvious? Probably. Is there a way we can lay out a 10-inch post that doesn't sound remedial or take a lot of time but st
Tigers gonna think their pressure worked

texts-pedro-gomez.title: Text Conversation with Journalist - Pedro Gomez (ESPN)
texts-pedro-gomez.context: Text message conversation with Journalist - Pedro Gomez (ESPN)

messages.message: How bad is Miggy?
Tigers have been playing well for a few months. Almost since Brad took his jacket off and covered the plate

Hey Pedro. He's a huge energy guy and has given them some much-needed speed at the top of the order. He also is conscious of hitting in front of Cabrera, and draws walks. But to me, biggest thing is his energy. They feed off it.

Here's an indication of how much more comfortable you are now than two years ago:
 

 "The Tigers are practicing bunt coverages and Miguel Cabrera can't stop talking. He's communicating in mid-season form."

Here's a Q for you: In sourcing and getting info. A NL team flew in a special assistant here to watch Verlander...They picked my brain. Is that something you would ever pass on to Tigers people, like Al, as an exchange of information of sorts?
Good as can be. Was sitting in my hotel writing this story when I saw you ...
http://www.freep.com/story/sports/mlb/tigers/2017/07/19/detroit-tigers-jd-martinez-trade/491015001/
Something absolutely couldn't have done two seasons ago. Still disappointed in getting beat by National guys, and I don't have a Tigers guy to help in a pinch but it's a work in progress
Very nice job on the trade story. Told your readers a ton.
I'm going to lose the clubhouse
Be careful man. Your gonna lose the clubhouse
Here's the thing, your career will outlast every single player in that clubhouse. You have to be strong. Plus, if you're not getting yelled at then you're probably not doing your job right.

This is definitely one of those situations for you. You have to be inside the clubhouse the moment it opens tomorrow. And you have to be there to let anyone who wants to vent. Just be prepared to back up your side. Remember, you don't work for the Tigers. You work for your readers.
I looked on freep.com. Couldn't find anything other than your news story on the suspensions. Did I miss it?
You're moving into a different category now. You're a serious reporter now, someone to be taken seriously from here on out.
Again, it is not easy to take this step. I know that. And if you decide to spike it, don't worry. If it's not where you want it, YOU make the call. It's your name on the story.
Do you have a link or text to that Schilling story?
Keep a good record of all the things he's been doing so that if he is traded you'll be ready with what he did to get himself traded
Schill got himself traded on deadline July, 2000.
Remember your fall-back: what was incorrect in my story?
